questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Crucial for my choice of exchange was the fact of going somewhere english speaking so that there would not be any type of language barrier. Also, as I have lived in Sydney in my early youth, I have always felt an urge of going back to Australia as a young adult and make use of the unique opportunity of trying to live abroad and immerse myself in new cultures, ways of living and establish a new network here in Melbourne. 
The overall motivation included the different academic oppurtunies UniMelb offers, also with regards to Film and Media. Here I have had four creative breadth courses that all have given me a better overview and helped me narrow down my overall interests for the field of film and photography. Specifically I had a micro documentary course, a street art course and a screenprinting course that all offered me the possibility of trying out new and prevalent interests in more hands-on and practical approach to learning and studying.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Overall I think the semester was very well structured, however towards the end of the semester everything got a little more intense as I was doing final assignments for all four courses at once which really forced me to prioritise the amount of energy used to finish them all. E.g. the documentary course was of my biggest interest, hence I disposed my time in perfecting those assignments. 
As I am normally used to only having two courses pr. semester (2x 15 ECTS points), this was a little more of a challenge as I had double the amount of courses whilst also working around 24 hours a week in order to sponsor my whole exchange semester abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very straight forward, given the fact that the UniMelb website (University of Melbourne) was very easy to navigate and they were good and communicating all the most essential information and steps for completing the enrolment. Also they were good and quickly responding on email to any relevant questions I had to the whole process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help to order my student id, enrol into subjects and/or change any courses I was unsure about.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Good orientation but not very personal. Very hectic, too many students. Maybe for the more social aspect of studying, each course I was studying could maybe have had a form of small introduction in order to socialise with other students. I am aware that this is costly, so all in all I think that UniMelb offered a lot of possibilites to meet other exchange students, however I had more of an idea to immerse myself and integrate myself with locals, hence the biggest network I have made from living here was through my work colleagues.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest, however some good Facebook groups for it like "Fairy Floss Estate". I found my sharehouse in North Melbourne through a friend of a friend who was living here the previous semester and then there was a smooth transition between us and me moving in.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would say it is a lot better and offers you the oppurtunity of living with people more locally immersed in Melbourne. However this question always depends on who your housemates are and how social they are to make the living situation comfortable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would say the prices were a lot more expensive than I had anticipated. Living with locals and finding a room on facebook would probably make the whole semester cheaper for the individual student.,

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy and with enough deadlines and reminders, not too forget to enrol and register in good time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty straightforward and the website of University of Melbourne really also made it easier. I know of people who have done exchange where it has been a lot more difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The messaging and mailing with Melbourne University and also with a contact person from my home institutition. Also zoom meetings and pdf documents sent through to assist the whole process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very smooth and my home institution also accepted the course list I sent through to them. However after arriving, within the first week of studies I ended up changing one of my courses as I found out it was planned to be active from end june till end july, which I did not realise before having spoken with a person at "Stop 1", UniMelbs study desk.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a good general idea of the courses, what the study load involves and also when the courses are planned out - what day of the week you study and when the first and final lecture is given. I had a course that I found out would run from end june till end july and immediately I wanted to change courses as the semester would only have been longer if i sticked to my initial four courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nice balance between academic litterature and theories together with practicality and creativity.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was content with the level of courses I ended up choosing for my semester at UniMelb. Street Art was a lot more academic than I initially thought, however I really enjoyed the lectures and the classroom discussion. Making Micro Documentaries was a very nice thought, some repetition with one of my previous courses at UCPH but I had anticipated it. Screenprinting was very interesting and I really enjoyed the different techniques we learned over the course of the 6 weeks of the intensive. Electronic Arts: Vision & Sound, was really something else and I kind of missed an overall structure and more clarity in the teaching and weeks of lectures. However, this can always be the case for breadth subjects as they often are not as academic and have a likelyhood of shifting a bit over the course of the semester

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers were very engaging and there was generally a good balance of interactivity, guest lecturers and also some field trips to cement the teaching and different theories. In my documentary course we unfortunately were taught online through zoom which really removed the personal aspect of teachings and interactions. Throughout the 12 weeks, it was not before the final week where we showed our productions that I got to actually have a feel about the course and who was partaking. I was among one of the only students that dared to "cam on", during the lectures and show myself instead of hiding "behind a computer screen", passively engaging.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Street Art (CCDP20001)
Making Micro Documentaries (FLTV10024)
Introduction to Screenprinting (FINA20045)
Electronic Arts: Vision & Sound (CCDP10002)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Street Art and Making Micro Documentaries I would recommend for future exchange students. If you are interested in subcultures I think that Street Art is a very interesting course to parttake in. Showcasing both local and international art, our teachers were very engaging and investing in doing their teachings. Also as Melbourne is globally known as one of the biggest hubs for Street Art and graffiti, I think this course is very relevant and interesting. 
Making Micro Documentaries I would also recommend as it was very well structured, the teachings were interesting and the assignments were very well spaced out and also challenged me to try filming and editing a micro documentary myself. I was very happy to have done this course and finally given it a go at doing all production and post-production of a movie myself. For future scenarios I will definitely use this skillset to make more films.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Visa was a lot more expensive than what we initially thought when applying and doing research in the autumn of 2023. Back then it cost around 3500,- dkk, however due to new immigration rules we were affected by the price increasing more than 100% where we ended up having to pay 7500,- dkk.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: If you buy yourself a bike you can definitely save a lot of money. I did not expect the infrastructure making it able to bike around the city in a way that could relate to Copenhagen. You can save a lot of money and time by investing in a nice bike for around 120 bucks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a lot of clubs, basically one for everyone on behalf of own personal interests.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Political clubs, tennis/football/gym clubs, mountaineering/bouldering clubs. Also film societies and other niche clubs that also had to do with food and cuisine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not end of joining any clubs, however in retrospect I would have loved to have joined the Mountaineering club. Primarily as it offered trips out of Melbourne to nature areas where you could explore and also try forces with bouldering together with other likeminded students. I have a friend that did it, and he was very satisfied with it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do some trips out the city, the infrastructure is good and it is easy to go explore other areas and also refresh a bit from living the metropolitan life. Melbourne has many good beaches (Sandringham etc) and also good nature areas such as Grampians and the Mornington Peninsula.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In my own opinion, being a very sociable and open person I think it was pretty easy. Also given the fact that I found a job as a waiter at nice Bar/restaurant, it really helped me boost my goal of immersing myself in local culture and make friends with locals.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be openminded and do not stress about not having enough friends. It is a process of learning to be more in your own company combined with many repetitive conversations about yourself and your background. It is so okay to just have a small friend group of 5-10 people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Did not really find any cultural differences compared to back home in Copenhagen. There is not really any language barrier and the cities are quite similar with regards to the gastronomy, music scene and also the love for the outdoors.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Especially the interest for music and gastronomy. Also how open and genuine Australians are. Always welcoming and asking about "how it is going". Some very friendly and polite aspects that I would love to bring back home and spread throughout Copenhagen. They are not judgy and actually put interest in learning about you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be well structured and organised with regards to your courses (important dates, weekly schedule, assignments etc)
2. Do not expect uni to be as social as back home, however it really depends on the courses you take and who you are studying with
3. Stay openminded, don't be too judgy and generally take initiative

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just keep an eye on your email and don't be afraid of writing too many emails.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely establishing a local network and having a normal looking week as back home with studies and work. Making friends with likeminded locals and also having the time to be more creative in my studies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably making friends at uni in your own classes and subjects. I think because of a general age-gap I did not immerse myself as much as I initially thought. However everyone is in the same position so just be open and take initiative. I was luckily blessed with nice housemates and good friends at work so I did not feel the urge to make friends at uni

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
